summary: Bruce B. Lawrence works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Fay School, Episcopal Divinity School, and Princeton University, and served at Duke University as Professor (~1971–2014) and later as Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Religion (~2014).

Bruce Charles Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.
Bruce Chilton works in religious studies. He studied at St John's College and held appointments at Yale University (~1985–1987) and Bard College, where he became Director (~1987).

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned his PhD at Columbia University (attested 1983) under Alex Wayman, also studying under Joel Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Kapferer is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Sydney and the University of Manchester under Max Gluckman, later holding posts at Adelaide, UCL, James Cook, Bergen, and Gothenburg.

Bruce Lincoln specializes in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Haverford College and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, he held posts at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago.
Bruce M. Sullivan specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen and held a post at Northern Arizona University from ~1988 to 2021.

Bruce Matthews works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. After graduate studies at McMaster University (~1970–1974), he held positions as a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Ceylon and as Professor of Comparative Religion at Acadia University (~1976–2007).

Bruce McCoy Owens specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held appointments at Columbia University (attested 1988) and Wheaton College (attested 2019 as associate professor of anthropology).

Bruno Dagens was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the EFEO (1969), KU Leuven (1972–1977), French Institute of Pondicherry (1977), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).
Bruno Galasek specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich was an Indologist who studied at Munich, Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn, and Breslau. He served as professor of Indology at the University of Breslau (1921–1928) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1921–1928).

Bruno Lindner was an Indologist who studied at the University of Leipzig (1871–1873) and under Rudolf von Roth (~1874–1878). He subsequently served as a Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig from 1878 to 1919.

Bruno Petzold studied at the Universities of Leipzig and Strasbourg, and under Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji. Working in Buddhist studies and Japanology, he taught at First Higher School, Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei Senior High School.
Bruno Schindler was a Sinologist who studied under August Conrady (~1912–1919). He founded the journal Asia Major in 1923 and later worked as a Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries (~1939–1964).

Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under Jacqueline I. Stone, among others, and held a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

Bryan J. Cuevas specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Emory University and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, later holding posts at Princeton University and Florida State University.

Bryan W. Van Norden specializes in philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1985–1991) and served as a professor in the philosophy and Chinese & Japanese departments at Vassar College (~1996–2021).
Bryce Ryan was a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon, where he taught Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah.

Bulcsu Siklós specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles Roskelly Bawden, later holding a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).
